mechanism: Both drugs possess anticholinergic properties; oxybutynin is a direct muscarinic antagonist while hydroxychloroquine has secondary anticholinergic effects, leading to additive anticholinergic toxicity.
action: Monitor for anticholinergic adverse effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, cognitive impairment, tachycardia); consider alternative antimuscarinic or adjust dosing if symptoms develop.
